tells.1: Emoji-heavy, bolded bullet format feels like a generic AI Slack template.
tells.2: Formal, wordy phrasing such as 'The date for changeover will be on' feels unnatural for a quick Slack update.
tells.4: Very tidy parallel bullets and chirpy tone feel slightly over-produced.
tells.6: Repeated 'On [date]' sentence openings make it feel mechanical.
tells.7: Terse, affectless bullet list with an uneven final item feels generated rather than voiced.

reason: Version 3 gives the best mix of clear dates, scannable formatting, and approachable tone for a team Slack post. Version 5 is very natural, but 3 is easier to scan and act on.
